messages.subject: Having difficulty configuring a scatter plot
parts:
Hi all,

Hadley suggested asking the group for assistance.

I eventually found a version of the WIN ggplot2 and installed.

I am having problems getting a scatter plot configured and have tried all the various syntax combinations and consulted every reference I can find w/o any help. I searched all examples on the ggplot web site and had no response from the general R help group.
It must be simple.  I am still going through all of Hadley's manuals and documents, but still struggling.
I assume using ggplot2 what I need can be achieved.

So I throw myself on your mercy for a bit of help.
This can be done in Excel, but not done well since the time axis on left is not correct.
Below is my R plot.




What I am plotting is activity time during the night for bats. But I only want the times displayed from 17:00 to 07:00 like the Excel example.
the problem with Excel is it does not deal well with the "Midnight" roll over issue so the plots and legend on left is "Time since previous noon" which does not make for intuitive plots for publication.

For my plots in R I need the time axis to only display fixed times from 17:00 to 07:00 and not the the blank day time gap.
The Excel plot has the scatter points centered around midnight 00:00 hours. I can not seem to be able to do this in R.

I need to generate hundreds of the same type of plot below.  Once I understand the syntax or code to a fixed time axis I think I can move forward so times are displaying correctly.  The dates and everything else can and will change with each data set.
Below is the current code for my R plots.

I can send a small DOC file with sample data and code if that is necessary if anyone out there can assist.

Cheers from the jungles of Belize,

Bruce
++++++++++++++++++++++++++++

messages.subject: Re: Having difficulty configuring a scatter plot
parts:
I wanted to graph something similar, and I have to admit that I
eventually just compromised and did the expedient thing (plotting
glucose numbers here, and wanted to start at 6 am):

a2 <- read.table ("Glucose.txt", sep="\t", header=T)
a2$when <- as.POSIXct (as.character(a2$when), tz="", format="%m/%d/%y
%H:%M")

h <- format(a2$when, "%H")
m <- format(a2$when, "%M")
hh <- as.numeric (h) + (as.numeric (m) / 60)
hh[hh<6] <- hh[hh<6] + 24

f <- data.frame (when=hh, glucose=a2$glucose)

x.lab = c("6a", "8a", "10a", "12p", "2p", "4p", "6p", "8p", "10p",
"12a", "2a", "4a", "6a")

(qplot (when, glucose, data=f, shape=I(1), geom=c("smooth", "point"),
span=0.66, degree=2,
main="Glucose 2008-03-04 through 2008-08-10")
+ scale_x_continuous ("Time", breaks=seq(6, 30, 2),
labels=x.lab)
+ scale_y_continuous ("Glucose", breaks=seq(0, 450, 50),
limits=c(0, 450)))

So basically, I turned the times into numbers instead of keeping them
dates. This plot started in lattice, though, so maybe there is a
better way to do it.

Wayne

parts:
Below I've included some handy date functions that I use. With them
you can remove the date component of a date time as follows:

year(mydate) <- 2000
yday(mydate) <- 1

then when you plot mydate, you'll only see a days worth of data
(getting the day to start at 6am would be a little trickier, however)

second <- function(x) as.POSIXlt(x)$sec
minute <- function(x) as.POSIXlt(x)$min
hour <- function(x) as.POSIXlt(x)$hour
yday <- function(x) as.POSIXlt(x)$yday + 1
wday <- function(x) as.POSIXlt(x)$wday + 1
mday <- function(x) as.POSIXlt(x)$mday
week <- function(x) yday(x) %/% 7 + 1
month <- function(x) as.POSIXlt(x)$mon + 1
year <- function(x) as.POSIXlt(x)$year + 1900
tz <- function(x) {
tzs <- attr(as.POSIXlt(x),"tzone")
tzs[length(tzs)]
}

"second<-" <- function(x, value) as.POSIXlt(x) - (second(x) - value)
"minute<-" <- function(x, value) as.POSIXlt(x) - (minute(x) - value) * 60
"hour<-" <- function(x, value) as.POSIXlt(x) - (hour(x) - value) * 3600
"yday<-" <- function(x, value) as.POSIXlt(x) - (yday(x) - value) * 3600 * 24
"wday<-" <- function(x, value) as.POSIXlt(x) - (wday(x) - value) * 3600 * 24
"mday<-" <- function(x, value) as.POSIXlt(x) - (mday(x) - value) * 3600 * 24
"week<-" <- function(x, value) as.POSIXlt(x) - (week(x) - value) * 3600 * 24 * 7
"month<-" <- function(x, value) {
ISOdatetime(year(x) + (value - 1) %/% 12, (value - 1) %% 12 + 1 ,
mday(x), hour(x), minute(x), second(x), tz(x))
}
"year<-" <- function(x, value) {
ISOdatetime(value, month(x), mday(x), hour(x), minute(x), second(x), tz(x))
}
"tz<-" <- function(x, value) {
ISOdatetime(year(x), month(x), mday(x), hour(x), minute(x), second(x), value)
}

Hadley
